findings.title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible.
findings.comment: FIRST REPEAT: Inspector observed the paper towel dispenser at the juice hand washing station to be non-operational. CORRECTED- the person in charge (PIC) informed maintenance, who cleared the jam in the dispenser. Ensure paper towels are always readily available to complete proper hand washing.
findings.citation_text: 6-301.12 Hand Drying Provision. Each HANDWASHING SINK or group of adjacent HANDWASHING SINKS shall be provided with: (A) Individual, disposable towels; (B) A continuous towel system that supplies the user with a clean towel; or (C) A heated-air hand drying device; or (D) A hand drying device that employs an air-knife system that delivers high velocity, pressurized air at ambient temperatures. [Pf]

findings.title: Thermometers are provided and accurate.
findings.comment: The standing cooler in the sampling prep room does not have an ambient thermometer. Ensure ambient thermometers are present at the front of cooling units to monitor the warmest temperature of the unit- which should be at or below 41F. Correct by next routine inspection.
findings.citation_text: 4-204.112(A) Temperature Measuring Devices. (A) In a mechanically refrigerated or hot FOOD storage unit, the sensor of a TEMPERATURE MEASURING DEVICE shall be located to measure the air temperature or a simulated product temperature in the warmest part of a mechanically refrigerated unit and in the coolest part of a hot FOOD storage unit. [C]

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
findings.comment: Inspector observed fragmented caulking behind the hand washing sink of the juice station. Maintain proper repair of physical facilities by resealing the sink to the wall by the next routine inspection.
findings.citation_text: 6-501.11 Repairing. PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be maintained in good repair. [C]

findings.title: Hands clean and properly washed.
findings.comment: Inspector observed food handler donning gloves before handling food. CORRECTED- education was provided regarding the need to wash hands prior to donning gloves. Ensure all employees wash hands before donning gloves.
findings.citation_text: 2-301.14 When to Wash. FOOD EMPLOYEES shall clean their hands and exposed portions of their arms as specified under § 2-301.12 immediately before engaging in FOOD preparation including working with exposed FOOD, clean EQUIPMENT and UTENSILS, and unwrapped SINGLE-SERVICE and SINGLE-USE ARTICLES and: (G) When switching between working with raw FOOD and working with READY-TO-EAT FOOD; (H) Before donning gloves to initiate a task that involves working with FOOD; and (I) After engaging in other activities that contaminate the hands. [P]

findings.title: Contamination prevented during food preparation, storage and display.
findings.comment: Sanitizer bottles were observed on the same shelf as the sampling orange juice on the cart. CORRECTED- employee moved the sampling juice to the counter. Education was provided regarding the need to separate toxic substances from ready to eat (RTE) food items. Ensure chemicals are stored away from RTE items to prevent potential contamination of food.
findings.citation_text: 3-307.11 Miscellaneous Sources of Contamination. FOOD shall be protected from contamination that may result from a factor or source not specified under Subparts 3-301 - 3-306. [C]

findings.title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible.
findings.comment: Ice and juice was observed in the basin of the juicing station handwashing sink. CORRECTED- Discussed with PIC and employee. Ensure handsinks are only used for handwashing (not used as a dump sink).
findings.citation_text: 5-205.11 Using a Handwashing Sink. (A) A HANDWASHING SINK shall be maintained so that it is accessible at all times for EMPLOYEE use. (B) A HANDWASHING SINK may not be used for purposes other than handwashing. [Pf]

findings.title: Food handler training
findings.comment:
1st REPEAT: One of the 3 employees present during this inspection has not completed food handler training. PIC discussed the training with the employee and checked that they have access to the training in the computer-based learning system. Ensure all employees complete food handler training within 30 days of hire and renew as needed.
410 ILCS 625/3.06(b). Food handler training: restaurants. (b) Unless otherwise provided, all food handlers employed by a restaurant, other than someone holding a food service sanitation manager certificate, must receive or obtain American National Standards Institute-accredited training in basic safe food handling principles within 30 days after employment and every 3 years thereafter. [C]

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
findings.comment: Spray bottle of sanitizer at both demo stations was observed at 0ppm quat. No sanitizer concentration could be detected from the wall-mounted dispenser at the 3 compartment sink, where both bottles would have been filled. PIC has contacted EcoLab to have them look at the wall-mounted dispenser. In the meantime, Crossmark staff will fill sanitizer spray bottles and do the few dishes they have to wash/rinse/sanitize at the 3 compartment sink in the Cafe.
findings.citation_text: 4-501.114  A quaternary ammonia compound solution shall be used in accordance with the EPA-registered label use instructions and be maintained at the concentration as indicated by the manufacturer's use directions included in the labeling. Use test strips to verify concentration. [P]

findings.title: All food employees have food handler training
findings.comment:
A food handler certificate was not available for one of the two employees serving samples during this inspection. Ensure all food employees complete food handler training within 30 days of hire (and renew as needed). Keep certificates available on file for review during health inspections.
410 ILCS 625 and IAC Section 750.3430 (C) Facility is not in compliance with the food handler law. All food handlers, other than someone who has the food service sanitation manager certificate, shall receive or obtain training in basic food handling principles as outlined in Subpart M of the Illinois Food Code. Food handlers working at a temporary food establishment are exempt from this requirement. [C]

findings.title: Procedures for responding to vomiting and diarrheal events
findings.comment:
Facility does not have a written clean up policy for vomit/diarrhea clean up on file. CORRECTED- Inspector provided a clean up policy. Keep written policy posted or on file for reference if needed.
2-501.11: A FOOD ESTABLISHMENT shall have written procedures for EMPLOYEES to follow when responding to vomiting or diarrheal events that involve the discharge of vomitus or fecal matter onto surfaces in the FOOD ESTABLISHMENT. The procedures shall address the specific actions EMPLOYEES must take to minimize the spread of contamination and the exposure of EMPLOYEES, consumers, FOOD, and surfaces to vomitus or fecal matter. [Pf]

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
findings.comment: Spray bottle of sanitizer at one demo station was observed at 100ppm quat. Solution was said to be prepared earlier in the day. CORRECTED- Fresh solution at 200ppm was provided. Solution freshly dispensed and two other spray bottles were confirmed to be at 200ppm.
findings.citation_text: 4-501.114  A quaternary ammonia compound solution shall be used in accordance with the EPA-registered label use instructions and be maintained at the concentration as indicated by the manufacturer's use directions included in the labeling. Use test strips to verify concentration. [P]

findings.title: Food separated and protected
findings.citation_text:
3-304.15(A) Employee touched the corner of their eye with gloved hands and did not change gloves prior to portioning a soup sample. Gloved hands were also wiped with a napkin instead of changing after soup splashed on hands while portioning. Proper glove use was discussed as well as periodic handwashing between glove changes. Employee changed gloves before continuing with next task.
Single use gloves shall be used for only one task, used for no other purpose, and discarded when damaged or soiled, or when interruptions occur in the operation.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
findings.citation_text:
4-602.11 & 4-702.11 Container used for storage of sliced cheese at demo station was held at room temperature. The same container was used for ~2.5hrs prior to employee’s lunch break. When asked about cleaning process for the container between morning and afternoon samples, employee noted the container was wiped out with water. Container was not properly cleaned and sanitized between uses but was briefly refrigerated for ~30 minutes while employee was on lunch break. Proper ware washing was discussed, and a clean container was provided for sample storage.
If used with time/temperate control for safety foods, equipment food contact surfaces and utensils shall be cleaned throughout the day at least every 4 hours. Utensils and food contact surfaces shall be sanitized before use after cleaning.

findings.title: Warewashing facilities: installed, maintained, & used; test strips
findings.citation_text:
4-303.11 Sanitizer spray bottle at soup demo station was empty. Employee noted they just ran out. Bottle was refilled with sanitizer at 200ppm. Ensure sanitizer solutions are maintained at demo station. If sanitizer runs out, ensure fresh solution is provided prior to continuing with operations. 
Sanitizer shall be provided and available for use during all hours of operation.

findings.title: Charge present, demonstrates knowledge, and performs duties
findings.citation_text:
2-102.11 (C)(2), (3) and (17) Priority violations were observed concerning handwashing and sanitization. Manager was educated and advised to ensure all staff are trained accordingly. 
Based on the risks inherent to the food operation, during inspections and upon request the PIC shall demonstrate to the regulatory authority knowledge of foodborne disease prevention, application of the hazard analysis and critical control points, and the requirements of the Code.

findings.title: Hands clean and properly washed
findings.citation_text:
2-301.11 Proper handwashing at the designated handwashing sink was not possible in the kitchen due to the absence of soap at the handwashing sink. Soap was provided during inspection (see #10).
Food employees shall keep their hands and exposed portions of their arms clean.

findings.title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible
findings.citation_text:
6-301.11 Soap was not available at the kitchen handwashing sink. Manger stated she observed soap to be absent upon arrival to work that morning but was off for the last couple days. Soap was provided during inspection. 
Each handwashing sink shall be provided with a supply of hand cleaning liquid, powder, or bar soap.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
findings.citation_text:
4-501.114 Spray bottle of sanitizer at one demo station was observed at 0ppm quat. Solution was said to be prepared earlier in the day. Fresh solution at 200ppm was provided. Solution freshly dispensed and two other spray bottles were confirmed to be at 200ppm. 
A quaternary ammonia compound solution shall be used in accordance with the EPA-registered label use instructions and be maintained at the concentration as indicated by the manufacturer's use directions included in the labeling. Use test strips to verify concentration.
Ensure spray bottles of sanitizer are checked with test strips to verify concentration and refreshed as needed prior to concentration becoming weak and ineffective.

findings.title: All food employees have food handler training
findings.comment:
410 ILCS 625  Sec. 3.06 Proof of food handler certifications were not available for any staff working at the time of inspection. All three people working demo stations were said to be employed with the company for longer than 30 days. PIC was advised to ensure employees are completing food handler certification within 30 days of hire date. All staff that are not certified food managers need to complete an online food handler certification course that is ANSI and IL approved. Copies of certifications need to be maintained on-site.
All food handlers, other than someone who has the food service sanitation manager certificate, shall receive or obtain training in basic food handling principles as outlined in Subpart M of the Illinois Food Code.

findings.title: Plumbing installed; proper backflow devices
findings.citation_text:
5-205.15 Leaks at the sprayer and faucet of the 3 part sink remain to be corrected. Repairs have been scheduled.
A plumbing system shall be maintained in good repair.

findings.title: Hands clean and properly washed
findings.citation_text:
2-301.12 Proper handwashing technique is not possible with the lack of cold water at this time. A temporary handwashing station with warm water will be provided to promote proper handwashing (see general comments for details).
Food employees shall properly wash their hands with the following procedure: (1) rinse under clean, running warm water; (2) apply soap; (3) rub together vigorously for at least 10 to 15 seconds; (4) thoroughly rinse under clean, running warm water; and (5) immediately follow the cleaning procedure with thorough drying. 
To avoid recontaminating hands, use a disposable paper towel or similar clean barrier when touching surfaces such as manually operated faucet handles on a handwashing sink.

findings.title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible
findings.citation_text:
5-205.11 Upon arrival the handsink was blocked by a box holding empty strawberry cartons. Box was moved to allow access to the handsink. 
Handwashing sinks are to be accessible at all times and used only for handwashing. Cease the practice of placing items on top of the handsink for any reason.

findings.title: Gloves used properly
findings.citation_text:
3-304.15 Food employee touched her hair with gloved hands and did not immediately remove gloves. Inspector advised on proper glove use. Gloves were changed prior to continuing with food prep.
Single use gloves shall be used for only one task, used for no other purpose, and discarded when damaged or soiled, or when interruptions occur in the operation.

findings.title: Hot and cold water available; adequate pressure
findings.citation_text:
5-103.12 Cold water is still not available at the fixtures in the kitchen. Both the 3 part sink and handsink are impacted by the issue. A part has been ordered to repair the issue (see general comments for details).
Hot and cold water under pressure shall be provided to all fixtures, equipment, and nonfood equipment that are required to use water.

findings.title: Gloves used properly
findings.citation_text:
3-304.15 Employee at sample station touched a sanitizer spray bottle with gloved hands and did not immediately remove gloves. Gloves were removed upon request of inspector. Manager was advised to reiterate proper glove use and handwashing between glove changes. 
Single use gloves shall be used for only one task, used for no other purpose, and discarded when damaged or soiled, or when interruptions occur in the operation.

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean
findings.citation_text:
4-602.13 The following non-food contact surfaces were observed to be soiled:
A) inside broiler pan of the oven (food debris/dust);
B) inside oven (carbon buildup);  and
C) stove top burners (splash/buildup).
Clean the aforementioned items daily/as needed.
Non-food contact surfaces shall be cleaned at a frequency necessary to eliminate buildup of grease, food splash and general debris.

findings.title: Hot and cold water available; adequate pressure
findings.citation_text:
5-103.12 Cold water was not available at the 3 part sink when the faucet was switched to allow for free flowing water. Manager explained work arounds that are used for washing produce (using ice to chill hot water) and filling the 3 part sink for ware washing (running detergent and sanitizer chemical lines at the same time to cool the water). A work order was placed during inspection. Both hot and cold water need to be available at the sink.
Hot and cold water under pressure shall be provided to all fixtures, equipment, and nonfood equipment that are required to use water.

findings.title: Plumbing installed; proper backflow devices
findings.citation_text:
5-205.15 Sprayer at 3 part sink does not currently work. A work order was placed for repairs during the inspection.
A plumbing system shall be maintained in good repair.
